questionText:
Consider the following augmented grammar with $\{\#, @, <, >, a, b, c\}$ as the set of terminals.

$$S' \rightarrow S$$
$$S \rightarrow S \# c S$$
$$S \rightarrow S S$$
$$S \rightarrow S @$$
$$S \rightarrow < S >$$
$$S \rightarrow a$$
$$S \rightarrow b$$
$$S \rightarrow c$$

Let $I_0 = \text{CLOSURE}(\{S' \rightarrow \bullet S\})$. The number of items in the set $\text{GOTO}(\text{GOTO}(I_0, <), <)$ is _______
explanation:
Step 1: Compute $I_0 = \text{CLOSURE}(\{S' \rightarrow \bullet S\})$
Since the dot is before non-terminal $S$, we add all productions of $S$ with the dot at the beginning:
$I_0 = \{$
$S' \rightarrow \bullet S$,
$S \rightarrow \bullet S \# c S$,
$S \rightarrow \bullet S S$,
$S \rightarrow \bullet S @$,
$S \rightarrow \bullet < S >$,
$S \rightarrow \bullet a$,
$S \rightarrow \bullet b$,
$S \rightarrow \bullet c$
$\}$

Step 2: Compute $I_1 = \text{GOTO}(I_0, <)$
Looking at items in $I_0$ where the dot is immediately before '$<$':
Only $S \rightarrow \bullet < S >$ yields the kernel item $S \rightarrow < \bullet S$.
Taking closure gives:
$I_1 = \text{CLOSURE}(\{S \rightarrow < \bullet S\}) = \{$
$S \rightarrow < \bullet S$,
$S \rightarrow \bullet S \# c S$,
$S \rightarrow \bullet S S$,
$S \rightarrow \bullet S @$,
$S \rightarrow \bullet < S >$,
$S \rightarrow \bullet a$,
$S \rightarrow \bullet b$,
$S \rightarrow \bullet c$
$\}$

Step 3: Compute $I_2 = \text{GOTO}(I_1, <)$
In $I_1$, the item with the dot before '$<$' is $S \rightarrow \bullet < S >$.
Moving the dot past '$<$' yields the kernel item $S \rightarrow < \bullet S$.
Thus, $I_2 = \text{CLOSURE}(\{S \rightarrow < \bullet S\}) = I_1$.

Since $I_2$ contains 8 items, the size of $\text{GOTO}(\text{GOTO}(I_0, <), <)$ is 8.
